domains.name: Information and Ideas
domains.desc: Understanding what a text says and what it proves.
skills: Finding the main point of a text and the facts that support it.
Completing a text with the conclusion that the evidence supports.
Choosing the quote, or the data in a table or graph, that supports or weakens a claim.

domains.name: Craft and Structure
domains.desc: How words and texts are built and why the author wrote them.
skills: Choosing the word that fits the meaning and tone of a sentence.
Seeing why an author wrote a passage, or a part of it, and how it is built.
Seeing how two short texts relate: agree, disagree or respond to each other.

domains.name: Expression of Ideas
domains.desc: Making writing clear, organised and effective.
skills: Using a list of notes to write a sentence that meets a stated goal.
Choosing the word or phrase that links two ideas logically.

domains.name: Standard English Conventions
domains.desc: The grammar and punctuation rules of formal English.
skills: Punctuation that joins or separates sentences and parts of sentences.
Verb tense, subject–verb agreement, pronouns, plurals and modifiers.

domains.name: Algebra
domains.desc: Lines, equations and systems: the engine of the Math section.
skills: Solving equations with one unknown, including no solution and infinitely many.
Slope, intercepts and what each number means in a real situation.
Writing and reading equations of lines with x and y.
Finding where two lines meet, or how many solutions they have.
Solving and graphing inequalities in one or two variables.

domains.name: Advanced Math
skills: Quadratic, exponential and other curves: reading and building them.
Solving equations with squares, and lines meeting curves.
Rewriting an expression in a different but equal form.

domains.name: Problem-Solving and Data Analysis
domains.desc: Numbers in real life: rates, percents and data.
skills: Proportions, speed, density and converting units.
Percent of, percent change and combined percents.
Mean, median, range and spread of a data set.
Scatterplots and lines of best fit.
The chance of events, including conditional probability from tables.
What a sample can and cannot tell us, and margin of error.
Judging whether a study supports its conclusion.

domains.name: Geometry and Trigonometry
skills: Angle rules, similar and congruent triangles.
Pythagoras, special triangles, sine, cosine and tangent.
Arcs, sectors, radius and the circle equation.
